a RELEASED tag on the public mirror cannot be silently MOVED. scripts/publish-public.sh force-pushed the tag (:286) while pushing main NON-force (:285) -- the commit history was protected from rewrite while the TAG, the only name an adopter ever pins to, could be moved out from under them. Now: publish_decision() is a PURE function encoding a PRECISE rule (tag absent -> publish; tag published + tree IDENTICAL -> noop, so the benign idempotent re-run STAYS GREEN and the gate never fires on the happy path; tag published + tree DIFFERS -> REFUSE, which is the actual defect: every adopter pinned to that tag would silently receive a tree they never audited). Underneath it, -f/--force are gone: a NON-FORCE tag push is rejected by git itself if it would MOVE a ref, which is the layer that still holds if a concurrent publish lands the tag between our clone and our push (the TOCTOU window the refusal alone cannot close). PROVEN, NOT ASSERTED: the selftest exercises a REAL local repo (no network, no creds) -- a non-force tag push REFUSES to move a published tag, AND --force DOES move it, so the first result is load-bearing rather than vacuous. HONEST CEILING: this binds the TOOL, the accident, and the agent. It does NOT bind a human with push rights doing `git push --force` by hand -- only a forge-side tag ruleset does (see mirror-tag-protection), and a repo ADMIN CAN LIFT THAT RULESET. Immutability is ENFORCED BY THE FORGE and merely ATTESTED here; we claim tamper-EVIDENT-and-deliberate, never tamper-proof.
